Hi Emily — great to hear. Quick heads-up on timing: the US moves to DST on Sun Mar 14 (ET becomes EDT, UTC-4) while our EU engineering team in Berlin stays on CET (UTC+1) until Mar 28. That window can cause confusion when converting local times, so I want to propose a few concrete slots that account for the DST shift.

A couple of options that usually work for cross-region demos:

Option A — mid-day for EU, early morning for US execs
- Mon Mar 15, 07:30am ET (EDT) / 12:30pm CET (Berlin) — good for EU devs, early for US PMs

Option B — later in US afternoon (exec-friendly) but late evening in EU
- Mon Mar 15, 05:00pm ET (EDT) / 10:00pm CET (Berlin) — possible but late for EU engineering team

Option C — earlier in week to avoid DST switch (Fri Mar 12)
- Fri Mar 12, 10:00am ET (EST) / 16:00 CET (Berlin) — before US DST starts, both sides are on the more stable offsets

Notes:
- On Mar 15 ET will be UTC-4; Berlin will be UTC+1.
- If execs want mid-day on ET (e.g., 12:00pm ET) that will be 17:00 CET — workable but can stretch into late afternoon for our engineers.

If you'd like, I can loop in Aditya (US-based SE) to present from the US side so we can avoid asking the EU engineers to join after 10pm.

I've attached a short 1-pager agenda and can send a calendar invite once we lock a time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager — Americas
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
